rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the primary uncertainty is the baseline performance level. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, least confounded configuration in the search space: a single modality, a single profile, and a standard linear encoder (PCA-2000). Establishing this floor first is critical because every subsequent experiment—whether testing multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders (scvi, scgpt), image modality, or multimodal fusion—needs a clean reference to measure improvement against. It isolates the RNA signal quality without introducing complexity from aggregation, learned representations, or fusion, making any future performance gains attributable to specific design choices rather than confounded by multiple simultaneous changes.

With only one data point (config_001: RNA-only/PCA/singleprofile at 48.5% accuracy), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries independent predictive signal. Testing config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image contribution without confounding from fusion or multiprofile aggregation, and uses the simplest image encoder for a clean comparison against the RNA baseline. If image accuracy is substantially higher or lower than 48.5%, it immediately clarifies whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing and which modality should anchor the model. If it is similar, the bottleneck is likely task difficulty rather than modality choice, redirecting effort toward RNA encoder improvements. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design axis (modality value) before committing limited budget to the much larger multimodal configuration space.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (resnet50, singleprofile) is only 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant signal and the primary avenue for improvement. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the multiprofile structure (multiple profiles per cell with aggregation) provides meaningful additional information over a single profile, or whether the bottleneck is encoder quality. This experiment (config_002) tests the simplest logical extension of our best result: same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) but multiprofile with avgpool aggregation. It isolates the effect of profile structure and aggregation while holding the encoder constant, giving a clean comparison to config_001. If multiprofile+avgpool improves accuracy, it validates the direction and justifies testing transformer aggregation next (config_003). If it doesn't help, it redirects focus toward better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt). With 7 experiments remaining, this single-variable change is the most information-efficient next step to reduce uncertainty about the profile/aggregation axis before committing to more complex multimodal or encoder-swap experiments.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large jump over config_001 (singleprofile, 0.485), confirming multiprofile aggregation is the most impactful design choice so far. Image-only (config_010, 0.208) is clearly weak. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for multiprofile RNA? config_003 is the exact same setup as config_002 but swaps avgpool for transformer, isolating a single variable. Why this is best: With 6 experiments remaining, establishing the optimal aggregation strategy for the dominant RNA modality is critical before investing in multimodal fusion experiments (configs 016-051). A clean pairwise comparison (config_002 vs config_003) will tell us which aggregation to carry forward, reducing uncertainty about a key architectural choice that affects all downstream multimodal configurations. It is a low-risk, high-information exploitation of the strongest signal in the history.

Evidence: config_002 (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, clearly outperforming singleprofile (0.485) and transformer aggregation (0.519). Image-only is very weak (0.208). The key untested variable is whether a learned/pretrained RNA encoder can improve over PCA in the best-performing profile+aggregation setup. This experiment tests scgpt (a large pretrained single-cell encoder) with multiprofile+avgpool, directly comparing against config_002 by changing only the encoder. This is the best use of the next slot because it isolates one critical design choice (encoder quality) while holding the two settings that already showed clear benefit (multiprofile, avgpool) constant. If scgpt substantially improves over PCA, the remaining 5 experiments can exploit scgpt-based multimodal configs; if not, we can rule out encoder as a major lever and focus on fusion or other factors.

The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc. Image alone is very weak (0.208), and transformer aggregation underperforms avgpool. The critical open question is whether adding the image modality to the strongest RNA configuration can improve upon 0.591, or whether the weak image signal will dilute the RNA signal. Config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the most direct and minimal extension of the best RNA-only finding: it keeps the exact RNA/profile/aggregation settings that produced 0.591 and adds only the image branch with the simplest fusion (concat). This isolates the effect of multimodal fusion without confounding changes to encoder or aggregation. If it improves, the remaining 4 experiments can optimize fusion strategy and image encoder; if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can spend remaining budget refining RNA-side choices.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 accuracy. The image-only baseline (0.208) is very weak, suggesting the image branch contributes limited signal. The key uncertainty is whether the concat fusion in config_018 is optimal or whether weighted fusion could better balance the strong RNA signal (0.591) with the weak image signal. Config_019 changes only the fusion method (concat → weighted) while keeping all other settings identical to config_018, providing a clean A/B comparison. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it is a minimal, single-variable test of the most immediate improvement lever on the current best configuration. If weighted fusion wins, we have a clear new best; if not, we eliminate that direction and can focus remaining budget on the image encoder (e.g., ViT-L) or other dimensions.

The current best is config_019 (0.639 acc, multimodal/multiprofile/pca_n2000/resnet50/avgpool/weighted). The image modality contributes ~4.8% over RNA-only but is the weakest component (image-only resnet50 = 0.208). Config_025 makes a single change—replacing resnet50 with the stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder—while keeping all other settings at their known-optimal values (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image encoder quality on multimodal fusion. If the stronger ViT-L features improve the image branch, the weighted fusion should benefit disproportionately since it can up-weight a more informative image representation. This is the highest-impact single-variable test available: it targets the weakest link in the current best pipeline, and with 2 experiments remaining, a successful result would establish a new best while leaving one experiment for a final refinement (e.g., testing transformer aggregation in config_027).

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.639 acc. Evidence strongly supports avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, multiprofile > singleprofile, and multimodal > RNA-only. The one untested dimension in this best setup is the RNA encoder: we've confirmed pca_n2000 > scgpt (0.591 vs 0.530 in RNA-only), but scvi_n200 has never been tested. Config_031 makes a single-variable change (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) from the current best, directly testing whether a different learned RNA representation could push accuracy above 0.639. This is the highest-value experiment because it isolates the RNA encoder effect in the already-optimized multimodal pipeline, and with only one experiment remaining after this, confirming or ruling out scvi_n200 in the best configuration is the most informative use of the budget.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.6776. Evidence shows the RNA encoder is the dominant driver (scvi_n200 >> pca_n2000 >> scgpt), weighted fusion > concat, avgpool > transformer, and multiprofile > singleprofile. The one untested dimension within the top-performing family is the image encoder: with pca_n2000, resnet50 (0.639) and imagenet_vit_l (0.635) were nearly identical, but their interaction with the stronger scvi_n200 RNA encoder is unknown. Config_037 makes a single clean change (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) from the current best, testing whether a larger, more expressive image backbone provides complementary signal that the ViT's global attention can better exploit alongside scvi_n200's learned latent representation. As the final experiment, exploiting the strongest known configuration with one well-motivated modification maximizes the chance of a marginal gain while avoiding the risk of a multi-variable change.
